races.name: Magners Original Cider Restricted Maiden Stakes (For Horses In Bands B, C And D) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Sand Sea
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner for the David & Nicola Barron yard, returning 14 days after finishing sixth and seventh on good and soft; only one run on good ground in two recent starts with no wins or places to show, making it hard to make a case without evidence of a gear change.

runners_data.name: Thistle Nil
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's record of 9 wins from 45 in the past 14 days is a significant trainer flag; a hold-up type whose two recent runs on comparable going both yielded nothing, but Goldie's current form is the key angle to note.

runners_data.name: Alpha Platoon
runners_data.note: Ryan Sexton rides this three-year-old whose only run came on soft ground, so the step to good is an unknown; a natural hold-up horse who will likely be absorbed into the pack in this slow-run race, meaning his true style will be blunted and his chance discounted accordingly.

runners_data.name: Tide Runner
runners_data.note: Lightly raced and unknown stylistically, with a single placed run over 5f on good ground; the step up to 6f on the same surface is logical but the 38-day absence for John & Sean Quinn means freshness is the key variable to watch.

runners_data.name: Brash
runners_data.note: David Barron's three-year-old has finished seventh in both his runs on going around today's conditions and goes naturally to the back; pushed into a midfield map position by the volume of hold-up horses, his racing style means he will struggle unless this race develops unusual late pace.

runners_data.name: Star With Purpose
runners_data.note: Wears a hood and has shown modest form over 6f, finishing third at best; a versatile type who could push forward in the absence of dominant pace, and John & Sean Quinn's 2/12 trainer strike rate over 14 days adds a mild positive angle.

runners_data.name: Stoneacre Joe
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's 11/115 trainer record over 14 days is strong in strike-rate context; four runs on good going from five starts with two placed efforts at 6f on good ground give him the most relevant form profile of any runner, and his natural hold-up style is better suited than most in a field full of closers.

runners_data.name: Le Puy
runners_data.note: Lucinda Russell and Michael Scudamore's three-year-old returns after 58 days, the longest absence in the field; placed on good ground over 7f suggests stamina is not an issue, but the hold-up style and the layoff are both factors to weigh against a contested sprint finish.

runners_data.name: Shatin Beauty
runners_data.note: Completely unknown — no published form and no days-since-last-run figure available; Linda Perratt's 0/7 trainer strike rate over 14 days is a concern, but the absence of any exposed form means this runner cannot be fully dismissed in a weak maiden.

races.paceDynamic: With no confirmed front-runner in the field, this 6f contest at Ayr is set to drift into a moderate gallop before erupting into a sprint finish in the final two furlongs. Tide Runner and Star With Purpose carry unknown or versatile style tags and may push forward early, but neither has the profile to drive a truly honest pace on their own. The result is likely a race that crawls through the early stages before a wall of horses quickens simultaneously in the straight, compressing the finishing order and making positional advantage secondary to raw speed and a clear run. This shape decisively favours horses with sharp acceleration and the ability to travel in a compact field — prominently-raced types who can sit just off the pace and pick up quickly hold the structural edge. The field contains more hold-up depth than the pace map can physically represent at the rear — Alpha Platoon, Brash, and Stoneacre Joe are genuine come-from-behind types shown in midfield, but in a race this slow-run they are most likely to find themselves drawn into the pack rather than holding true back-marker positions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sprint Finish Suits Hangers-On
scenarios.trigger: If the pace drifts and the field bunches, producing a compressed sprint home from the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: If the pace drifts and the field bunches, producing a compressed sprint home from the two-furlong pole.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Two Steal The Rail
scenarios.trigger: If Tide Runner or Star With Purpose push forward and establish a small lead, converting the rail advantage on the straight course.
scenarios.body: If Tide Runner or Star With Purpose push forward and establish a small lead, converting the rail advantage on the straight course.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Hit Empty Wall
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is so slow that the backmarkers are traffic-bound as the field suddenly accelerates in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If the early pace is so slow that the backmarkers are traffic-bound as the field suddenly accelerates in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Open Maiden Lottery
scenarios.trigger: If the field fans wide in the straight and the race becomes a pure test of raw ability with no positional advantage playing a role.
scenarios.body: If the field fans wide in the straight and the race becomes a pure test of raw ability with no positional advantage playing a role.

watchPoints.text: Stoneacre Joe holds the most relevant turf form in the field — two placed runs at 6f on good ground — and Tim Easterby's yard is in strong form; watch whether Sean Kirrane can secure a clear passage in a compressed finish.

Tide Runner has been off 38 days and steps up from 5f to 6f for the first time; if Billy Garritty pushes forward early to replicate the placed run, the stamina question over the extra furlong becomes the pivotal factor.

Alpha Platoon and Brash are both genuine hold-up horses mapped into midfield due to overcrowding at the rear — in a slow-run sprint finish neither will be racing in their natural role, which structurally reduces their effectiveness and increases their exposure to traffic trouble.

Jim Goldie's yard is operating at 9/45 over the past 14 days, which stands out in this field; Thistle Nil has not placed in two recent runs but the trainer form angle makes it worth monitoring in the betting market.
Shatin Beauty has no public form whatsoever — watch the market moves closely, as any significant support for this runner would be the only meaningful signal available before the race.

races.name: AU Signature Handicap

runners_data.name: Penelope's Sister
runners_data.note: Best form has come over 8f on Good and Soft, and the step up to 1m2f is an open question; Jim Goldie's yard is in reasonable form at 7/30 over 14 days, Lauren Young claims 5lb, and two wins on similar going in the last 15 runs give her a platform, though the hold-up style means she needs something to go wrong up front.

runners_data.name: Dingwall
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer whose recent form string of 222 at 9-10f on Good is highly relevant here; Cara Tuke's 7lb claim helps offset the weight, Iain Jardine's yard is ticking over at 4/20 over 14 days, and tracking Myrrh from second position is precisely the role that suits this horse's natural pattern.

runners_data.name: Tap Dancer
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who has not won on Good going in recent runs and whose last win in similar conditions came from a limited sample; Paul Mulrennan is a quality booking but the 30-day absence and indifferent recent form at 8-11f make it hard to see a route to the front from this position.

runners_data.name: Elizabeth Bay
runners_data.note: In truth a genuine hold-up horse whose recent form includes a 3rd at 8f on Good, but the field congestion at the rear means she is unlikely to find her natural position; Katie Scott's yard has been quiet (0/10 over 14 days), and the last two runs show finishing positions of 8th and 9th, which makes the task from a compressed midfield difficult.

runners_data.name: Glasses Up
runners_data.note: An 11-year-old with two wins on Good going and 12/15 sim-going runs demonstrating course-type suitability, though the true closing style is compromised by redistribution into a more forward-mapped position; R Mike Smith's yard is quiet at 0/7, and the last run of 6th over 13f on Good suggests fitness is present even if the trip drops back slightly.

runners_data.name: Off Spin
runners_data.note: Four places from recent runs is a strong consistency flag, and the Tim Easterby yard firing at 8/91 over 14 days is a significant trainer angle worth noting; the tongue-tie is applied, Good going suits (3/10f on Good most recently), but being a true hold-up type squeezed forward on the map means the clean run she needs from the rear may not materialise cleanly.

runners_data.name: Myrrh
runners_data.note: The race's sole front-runner and the fulcrum around which the entire pace shape revolves; David O'Meara's yard is active at 8/52 over 14 days, David Nolan is a quality rider, and the 3-year-old has a win at 8f and recent placed efforts at 10-12f on Good — the solo lead on a flat, fair track is a significant tactical advantage, though the [STYLE_FIT=0.93] flag notes she has been mapped slightly out of pure role.

runners_data.name: Fans Favourite
runners_data.note: Won most recently over 9f on Soft and placed at 8f on Good, and the Hugo Palmer yard is active at 7/37 over 14 days; a natural hold-up horse whose proximity headgear (noted: hg:p) may help her travel closer to the pace than her style suggests, giving her a better chance than most closers in this shape.

runners_data.name: Shifter
runners_data.note: A 7-year-old whose form figures of 9-9854 are concerning, and the last two runs on Soft and Soft/Heavy show finishing positions of 8th and 9th; Wilf Storey's yard is very quiet (0/2 over 14 days), and the horse's true closing style is further hampered by the redistribution, leaving little in the profile to inspire confidence.

runners_data.name: Zebra Star
runners_data.note: Form figures of 050-95 on a variety of going types paint a picture of a horse in modest form, and the last Good-going run produced a 10th of 15; the hold-up style is genuine but the redistribution forward on the map means the horse is unlikely to get the clear passage from deep that its running style demands, and the R Mike Smith yard is silent at 0/7 over 14 days.

races.paceDynamic: Myrrh is the sole confirmed front-runner and, drawn in a field of largely hold-up horses, should stride into an uncontested lead from the outset and set a controlled, honest gallop over this 1m2f trip on Good turf at Ayr. Dingwall is the only genuine prominent type capable of tracking Myrrh, but with no other horse likely to press for the early lead, the pace will be sustainable and the race will be run to suit a horse that can travel close to the speed. The hold-up battalion — Elizabeth Bay, Glasses Up, Off Spin, Shifter, Zebra Star and others — are all true closers who have been redistributed forward on the map simply because there are more rear-end types than the race shape can accommodate at the back; in reality, they will attempt to close from off the pace but face a stiffer task if Myrrh is allowed to dictate without pressure. This race shape strongly favours horses racing prominently, with Myrrh able to control tempo and Dingwall the primary beneficiary of sitting closest to the pace-setter; genuine closers are operating against the grain of the race unless the tempo quickens sharply late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Myrrh Controls, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Myrrh sets a comfortable lead and the hold-up horses fail to close the gap from off the pace.
scenarios.body: If Myrrh sets a comfortable lead and the hold-up horses fail to close the gap from off the pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Myrrh Weakens, Closer Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Myrrh's controlled lead proves a fraction too fast over 1m2f and she fades in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: If Myrrh's controlled lead proves a fraction too fast over 1m2f and she fades in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Dingwall Tracks And Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Dingwall travels smoothly in Myrrh's slipstream and quickens past her in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: If Dingwall travels smoothly in Myrrh's slipstream and quickens past her in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaotic Pace, Outsider Lands It
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is misjudged and the race descends into a messy, falsely-run contest that scrambles the form.
scenarios.body: If the early gallop is misjudged and the race descends into a messy, falsely-run contest that scrambles the form.

watchPoints.text: Myrrh has the race entirely to herself up front — if David Nolan travels unopposed at a fair clip, watch for her simply never being headed, as no other runner has the pace profile to go with her early.

Off Spin has placed four times in recent runs and Tim Easterby's yard is firing (8/91 over 14 days); if she secures an unobstructed run from midfield late, she is the most dangerous closer in the race despite her compromised positional situation.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up types — Elizabeth Bay, Glasses Up, Shifter, Zebra Star — are all likely to fan wide in the straight searching for gaps; watch for interference or traffic issues in the final two furlongs as six genuine closers attempt to close on a front-runner who has had a clean lead.

Fans Favourite is the only hold-up horse with headgear (prominent) that may encourage her to race closer than her style suggests — if she travels in behind Dingwall rather than dropping out, her recent winning form makes her a live each-way danger worth tracking through the race.

Dingwall's consistent placing record (three 2nds in recent starts) raises the question of whether she can convert — Cara Tuke's 7lb claim is an asset but watch whether the mare jumps cleanly and secures her natural tracking berth, as losing that position early would significantly reduce her chance.

races.name: Millar Callaghan Engineering Handicap

runners_data.name: The Gay Blade
runners_data.note: In outstanding form having won twice in four days at this trip on good, with Andrew Mullen booked for an in-form Iain Jardine yard on a 4-day turnaround; his prominent style suits this race shape perfectly and he has the course and distance profile to press Black Storm from the outset.

runners_data.name: Novak
runners_data.note: Iain Jardine's stable is in excellent form (T14: 4/34) and this horse placed at 7f good recently, but his true role is hold-up and in a race where the pace map is already crowded with closers he is likely to find himself racing further back than ideal with less ground-making opportunity than his best effort suggests.

runners_data.name: Imperial Guard
runners_data.note: Michael Dods runner who has slipped to OR 62 after a sequence of finishing positions largely in the 6-9 range; he wants to race from off the pace but has been drifting back through the weights without converting, and stepping back up to 7f on good going hasn't unlocked him previously — each of his last five runs has been on 5f or 6f.

runners_data.name: Defence Missile
runners_data.note: A juvenile with just six starts and a 314-day absence, trained by Eve Johnson Houghton and ridden by 7lb claimer Finlay Bassett; the lengthy layoff and inexperience are the dominant flags here, and while he holds finishing positions in the mid-range, his natural hold-up style will be squeezed further by the crowded rear of this field.

runners_data.name: Al Muqdad
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's six-year-old has David Nolan aboard — a senior jockey positive — and has placed twice in similar going, running 3rd at 7f good most recently; he wears a hood and prefers to sit off the pace, which makes him one of the most legitimate closer threats in a field where many supposed hold-up horses are less genuine in that role.

runners_data.name: Ashen
runners_data.note: Won last time at 7f good and is clearly at home on this surface and trip for Jim Goldie; despite his hold-up tendencies he has the engine to push forward when conditions suit, and Paul Mulrennan may position him closer to the pace than his tag implies, making him one of the more dangerous runners if he secures a better position than expected.

runners_data.name: Dorney Lake
runners_data.note: Liam Bailey's five-year-old wears tongue-strap and has struggled to make an impact, finishing 5th or worse in all five recent starts on 6f good ground — this step up to 7f is a change, but his finishing efforts have not suggested he is waiting for a longer trip; the modest trainer strike-rate (T14: 1/5) adds little confidence.

runners_data.name: Black Storm
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed pace-setter who has gone clear front or prominent in recent 7f runs, finishing 2nd most recently on good; Katie Scott's light strike-rate (T14: 1/8) is a mild negative, but the tactical situation is entirely in his favour — an unchallenged lead on flat Ayr turf over a trip he handles is his best-case scenario and he controls how this race is run.

runners_data.name: Glorious Kitty
runners_data.note: Won back-to-back on good ground including a 7f success, and her form figures of 9-2511 are the most progressive in the field; the Easterby yard has a solid 14-day strike-rate and 7lb claimer Lewis Chalkley could be seen as a slight concern, but Glorious Kitty's raw ability and in-form profile make her one of the most credible threats even if she prefers to race closer than her hold-up tag suggests.

runners_data.name: Catalyse
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's other runner carries the ⚠ fade flag and has produced finishing positions of 7, 13, 10, 10, 9 in recent starts — there is no recent evidence of a winning or placing run despite the form string showing a past win; having raced just two days ago (LR: 2d) adds fatigue concern, and his tendency to fade late makes him a significant risk even if he gets into contention briefly.

races.paceDynamic: Black Storm is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival capable of disputing the lead, Ryan Sexton should be able to dictate from the front at a comfortable, controlled tempo over Ayr's flat 7f. The chasing pack behind is dominated by hold-up horses — Ashen, Dorney Lake, Novak, Imperial Guard, Defence Missile, Al Muqdad and Glorious Kitty all prefer to race off the pace — meaning Black Storm faces no early pressure and can set whatever fractions suit. The Gay Blade is the only other runner with a prominent profile and will likely track Black Storm into second or third, providing a natural buffer between the leader and the backmarkers. This race shape — a single, uncontested leader setting a fair gallop on good ground — strongly favours prominent racers who can travel close to the pace throughout and pounce in the straight, rather than true hold-up types who will need the tempo to accelerate sharply late, which an unchallenged leader is unlikely to generate. The field contains substantially more hold-up horses than the pace map can honestly accommodate at the rear; of those, Ashen and Glorious Kitty are the most likely to push forward and secure a better position than their natural style implies, while Novak, Dorney Lake, Defence Missile and Imperial Guard are the most likely to find themselves racing genuinely out of position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Black Storm Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Black Storm is allowed to dictate a sustainable gallop without any rival attempting to match him early.
scenarios.body: If Black Storm is allowed to dictate a sustainable gallop without any rival attempting to match him early.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Go With It
scenarios.trigger: If The Gay Blade pushes hard to match Black Storm's tempo and a genuine pace duel develops through the first half of the race.
scenarios.body: If The Gay Blade pushes hard to match Black Storm's tempo and a genuine pace duel develops through the first half of the race.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the straight, creating a sprint finish that rewards the deepest closer in the field.
scenarios.body: If the pace collapses in the straight, creating a sprint finish that rewards the deepest closer in the field.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Black Storm's early dominance lulls the field into a slow burn before the tempo suddenly spikes in the final 2f, causing a scrambled finish.
scenarios.body: If Black Storm's early dominance lulls the field into a slow burn before the tempo suddenly spikes in the final 2f, causing a scrambled finish.

watchPoints.text: Black Storm's early sectionals are critical — if Ryan Sexton is allowed to bowl along uncontested and sets a moderate pace, the rail position and control of the race make him a genuine danger throughout; monitor whether The Gay Blade attempts to press him or sits in behind.

Glorious Kitty and Ashen are both in strong recent form but will need their jockeys to push forward early to avoid being swallowed up by the pack of hold-up horses behind; if either gets trapped wide or deep in the field, their finishing speed may not be enough against a well-rested leader.

Catalyse ran just two days ago and carries a documented tendency to fade in the finish — if he is prominent at any stage, watch for him to drop away sharply inside the final 2f and potentially impede runners coming through.

Defence Missile returns from a 314-day absence as a juvenile taking on older horses — his behaviour in the early stages under a 7lb claimer is worth monitoring, particularly given the crowded hold-up section of this field may cause interference if he runs green.

The Gay Blade's fitness after a 4-day turnaround on similar ground is a positive angle, but if Andrew Mullen chooses to use him prominently to test Black Storm rather than track him, the pace dynamic of the entire race shifts and the hold-up brigade gain a much better chance of landing a blow late.

races.name: Tennent's Lager Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Obito
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with two placed efforts in his last four on Good ground and strong similar-going record (12/14 sim-going hits); David Nolan's positional awareness suits a horse who needs to lead, and 15 days since his last run is a fresh enough return — the [STYLE_FIT] tag reflects that he is listed as Prominent but will likely lead, which is actually his most advantageous role here.

runners_data.name: Cisco Disco
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old who has won three of his last five, including back-to-back wins on Heavy and Soft, so a drying Good surface is a mild concern; Oisin McSweeney takes the ride for a trainer whose 14-day strike rate is poor (0/16), and his prominent style should see him travel comfortably just behind Obito, but the going is quicker than his recent winning conditions.

runners_data.name: Livonian
runners_data.note: Ran in a tongue-tie last time and has shown ability over 1m on Good at Goodwood (a win), suggesting the step back up to 1m2f on similar ground is workable; Barry Murtagh sends him out with zero runners in the last 14 days suggesting a quiet operation, and his prominent style fits the likely race shape, though his recent form figures of 00 are hard to ignore.

runners_data.name: Star Cast
runners_data.note: In excellent recent form with four wins or placings in his last six starts over 10f on varying going including Good, and a 7lb claiming apprentice in Jake Dickson(7) represents a significant weight advantage; he is a natural prominent racer who has won over today's trip and going, making him one of the best-aligned horses to the predicted race shape — freshness is no concern at just 7 days between runs.

runners_data.name: Mr Lincoln
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who has placed at distances as long as 17f, so stamina is not a worry, but his best figures have come on Soft rather than Good and his sim-going record (0W2P) reflects that; Andrew Mullen takes the ride and trainer Iain Jardine has a modest 14-day record (4/26) — he needs the pace to lift substantially late and the race shape may not deliver it.

runners_data.name: Dwindling Funds
runners_data.note: Strong recent sim-going profile (9/15 hits, 3W5P) and a natural front-runner who has won over today's trip, but the congested prominent group means he will be pushed out of his comfort zone into midfield — his chance is genuinely compromised by the race shape, which is the honest read regardless of his raw ability; Paul Mulrennan is a high-quality booking if he does secure a prominent berth.

runners_data.name: Spanish Hustle
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old hold-up horse whose last six runs show finishes of 12th, 10th, 8th, 4th, and 4th — consistency of minor placing but no win since his form string suggests — and his sim-going profile (10/15, 1W3P) shows he handles Good; Amie Waugh's 3lb claim helps the weight, but the horse needs a strong gallop that this field is unlikely to generate in the straight.

runners_data.name: Pol Roger
runners_data.note: Has a recent placed run over 10f on Good (2nd) which is the most relevant positive in his form, but that is surrounded by out-of-the-money efforts and he has struggled on faster surfaces at Goodwood and York; Rhys Elliott's 5lb claim softens the burden and a hold-up style could theoretically suit a strongly-run race, but his inconsistency makes him a risky proposition.

runners_data.name: Molinari
runners_data.note: Long 188-day absence is a significant concern and all five of his recent runs have come on Tapeta (Standard), meaning today's Good turf is completely unknown ground for him in recent form — Billy Garritty rides for Martin Todhunter whose 14-day record is thin (1/2, too small to be meaningful); his natural prominent tendency will be squeezed by the packed front group, compounding an already difficult return from a long layoff.

runners_data.name: Sanafi Zabeel
runners_data.note: Has won on Good and placed on Good twice in his last three starts over 8-9f, showing he handles the surface — the step up to 1m2f is a query but not a disqualifier; Lauren Young's 5lb claim helps and Jim Goldie's yard is in decent form (7/42 in 14 days), but his true prominent style cannot be satisfied today given the front-running traffic ahead of him, and he will need to adapt quickly.

races.paceDynamic: Obito is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with only one horse likely to dominate up front, he should secure an uncontested lead and set a sustainable, metronomic gallop on Good ground over 1m2f at Ayr. Behind him, Cisco Disco, Livonian, and Star Cast are the natural prominent types who will jostle for the positions directly behind, creating a coherent and orderly early shape rather than a blistering pace. This field holds more prominent-minded runners than the race can accommodate at the front — Dwindling Funds, Molinari, and Sanafi Zabeel are true prominent racers who will be squeezed into midfield positions against their instincts, meaning they will not get the tactical comfort their style demands. A controlled, single-file pace with one leader and a contested prominent group suits horses with proven tactical speed who can sit just behind the pace and quicken from the second-last furlong — the patient hold-up types will face a searching finish if the pace is not strong enough to stretch the field, and the genuine front-runner profile of Obito must be respected throughout.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Obito Dictates, Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Obito leads unchallenged at a fair gallop and the pace is not hot enough to drain his stamina before the turn.
scenarios.body: If Obito leads unchallenged at a fair gallop and the pace is not hot enough to drain his stamina before the turn.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Trackers Swamp Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Star Cast or Cisco Disco press Obito hard enough in the back straight to lift the tempo and crack him.
scenarios.body: If Star Cast or Cisco Disco press Obito hard enough in the back straight to lift the tempo and crack him.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Pick Up Pieces
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo rises sharply in the middle stages and the prominent pack burns each other out.
scenarios.body: If the tempo rises sharply in the middle stages and the prominent pack burns each other out.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistribution Chaos Scrambles Field
scenarios.trigger: If the three displaced prominent types — Dwindling Funds, Molinari, Sanafi Zabeel — all push forward early and cause an unusually hot early pace.
scenarios.body: If the three displaced prominent types — Dwindling Funds, Molinari, Sanafi Zabeel — all push forward early and cause an unusually hot early pace.

watchPoints.text: Obito's uncontested lead is the fulcrum of the entire race shape — if anything forces him to race faster than his natural rhythm in the first half-mile, monitor whether his stride shortens noticeably entering the home straight, as that would trigger Scenario B and open the door for Star Cast and Cisco Disco.

Star Cast is 7 days between runs with strong course-and-distance form and a 7lb claimer taking off weight — watch for him to be produced with a forceful move rounding the final bend, as his profile fits the dominant shape almost perfectly.

Dwindling Funds, Molinari, and Sanafi Zabeel are all natural front-runners who cannot get their position — watch the first two furlongs for a crowded, scrimmaging start as these three instinctively try to push forward against the race shape, which could temporarily lift the tempo and cause interference.

Mr Lincoln and Pol Roger are both hold-up horses whose chances hinge on the pace being truly strong — if the early sectionals from Obito are visibly slow, discount both before the race has properly developed, as they will lack the room to close on a coasting front-runner.

Molinari's 188-day absence combined with an all-Tapeta recent profile means his early behaviour in the parade ring and stalls is worth monitoring — any signs of rustiness or reluctance would confirm that a significant price is not justified on form or fitness grounds.

races.name: Outcider Handicap

runners_data.name: Approaching Dawn
runners_data.note: Won over 8f on Good most recently and has the clearest form rationale for this trip and going; a natural hold-up horse who, despite being shown in midfield on the map due to the crowded rear, will want to come from off the pace — Lauren Young's 5lb claim is a genuine help on 127lbs.

runners_data.name: Walk On Walk On
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with headgear and a tendency to race lazily, form figures suggest nothing better than a fourth from nine outings; his natural inclination is to come from behind but the weak pace here may push him closer to the front than connections would prefer.

runners_data.name: Flying Moonlight
runners_data.note: Has run seven times in a row for minor positions — every one — with a 261-day absence and restricted to three Good/near-Good runs in the book; the layoff is a significant query and nothing in the form suggests a turnaround is imminent.

runners_data.name: Carmel Valley
runners_data.note: Unraced style marker (U) making him the biggest tactical unknown in the field; three runs at 7f on Good and Heather going have produced three finishes of 6th or worse, so stepping up to 1m on a track he's not visited is speculative.

runners_data.name: Hunterian
runners_data.note: Most consistent horse in the field with a form string of -23632 and multiple placed efforts at 8f — his best work comes at today's distance and the Good surface brings no concern; Charlie Johnston yard is in decent order at T14 6/47, and Andrew Mullen rides well from hold-up positions.

runners_data.name: Golden Valour
runners_data.note: Decade-old veteran running with headgear, bringing the most Good-ground experience of the redistributed hold-up types (10 runs, 1W2P); his natural style is come-from-behind but the map has him in midfield — R Mike Smith's T14 of 0/10 gives no trainer confidence boost here.

runners_data.name: Mayor Of Maghera
runners_data.note: Has been campaigned almost entirely over distances of 16f-20f in his recent history, making this 1m trip a dramatic drop in distance; the 3/9f on Good in his most recent run is mildly encouraging but the distance question dominates any assessment of his chance.

runners_data.name: Rory's Gold
runners_data.note: Ran just five days ago (6th over 7f Good), so bounce factor is a legitimate concern carrying 141lbs; the 3lb claimer Amie Waugh reduces the impost slightly, and his best form at 8f on Tapeta is not directly comparable to today's turf conditions.

runners_data.name: Braes Of Doune
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner back after 399 days off — his Good-ground form at 7f-9f is genuinely strong (2W8P from 12 runs on sim going) and the uncontested lead is a decisive tactical gift; the layoff is the only real caveat, and Jim Goldie has returned horses from long breaks successfully before.

races.paceDynamic: Braes Of Doune is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner 1m handicap at Ayr on Good ground, and with no other genuine pace horse to press him, he should be allowed to dictate a controlled, sustainable tempo from the front. The bulk of the field — Approaching Dawn, Walk On Walk On, Flying Moonlight, Golden Valour, Hunterian, Mayor Of Maghera and Rory's Gold — are all natural hold-up types, meaning the race will be strung out in pursuit of a lone leader setting a measured pace with minimal early friction. This field contains more hold-up and come-from-behind types than the race map can accommodate at the rear; of those redistributed to midfield on the map, Walk On Walk On and Golden Valour are the most likely to push forward and secure a prominent berth in the early stages given their headgear and tactical profiles. The resulting race shape — a lone leader, a steady pace, and a field of closers unlikely to get a true fast pace to chase — strongly favours patient hold-up horses who can produce a sustained finishing effort in the final two furlongs, provided Braes Of Doune doesn't simply steal it from the front.

scenarios.title: Braes Of Doune Front Steals
scenarios.trigger: If Braes Of Doune is allowed to dictate an uncontested, moderate pace and the hold-up field is left with too much ground to make up in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: If Braes Of Doune is allowed to dictate an uncontested, moderate pace and the hold-up field is left with too much ground to make up in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.body: If Braes Of Doune sets enough of a pace that true hold-up horses can produce a telling late run from off the back of the field in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Assert
scenarios.trigger: If Walk On Walk On or Golden Valour push forward to track Braes Of Doune closely and the race develops into a two-pace affair with the hold-up horses caught flat-footed.
scenarios.body: If Walk On Walk On or Golden Valour push forward to track Braes Of Doune closely and the race develops into a two-pace affair with the hold-up horses caught flat-footed.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos In The Pack
scenarios.trigger: If the redistributed hold-up horses contest positions early, causing interference or an uneven gallop that bunches the field and produces a rough race with a fortuitous winner.
scenarios.body: If the redistributed hold-up horses contest positions early, causing interference or an uneven gallop that bunches the field and produces a rough race with a fortuitous winner.

watchPoints.text: Braes Of Doune's 399-day layoff is the single biggest danger to the dominant scenario — watch whether Paul Mulrennan allows him to stride on freely or sits behind the bridle early, as any sign of reluctance to go forward immediately changes the race shape.

Walk On Walk On and Golden Valour both carry headgear and may push forward earlier than their natural style suggests — if either tracks Braes Of Doune closely from the off, the rear of the field loses its target pace and hold-up horses face a significantly harder task.

Mayor Of Maghera has run almost exclusively over 16f-20f recently; watch whether David Nolan elects to ride him positively over this much shorter 1m trip, which would be a significant change of approach and could further crowd the prominent positions.

Hunterian runs for the second time in nine days — monitor market moves at the off, as Charlie Johnston often runs horses back quickly when they are in peak condition and a market move would signal stable confidence in a horse already boasting the most consistent recent form in the field.

Carmel Valley is the only runner with a completely unknown style profile (U) — with Oisin McSweeney aboard and no tactical data to draw from, he is the wild card for positioning in the early stages and worth tracking out of the stalls to see whether he breaks forward or settles mid-division.

races.name: Mills Milk Scotland Handicap

runners_data.name: Laravie
runners_data.note: Recent course-and-distance winner who has won twice at 16-17f on Good going and shaped as though this trip and surface are ideal; Conor Whiteley's 7lb claim is an asset, and while she is mapped as Prominent her form strongly suggests she is the natural frontrunner here who has been running in a role slightly below her natural position on the pace map.

runners_data.name: Gallus Norman
runners_data.note: Paul Mulrennan takes a typically strong hold-up ride from the back, and Gallus Norman's best recent form has come at 13-16f on Good ground, making the surface and distance both genuine positives; Jim Goldie's yard is ticking over at 7/30 in the 14-day window and the 15-day freshener looks adequate.

runners_data.name: Ned Broy
runners_data.note: Stepped back up in trip after a modest recent run at shorter; his historical Good-going record in this sim-going profile is thin (0W1P from nine) and only one run at 18f suggests stamina for the full 1m7f is unproven at this level, with Lauren Young's 5lb claim a minor compensation.

runners_data.name: Fleur De Mer
runners_data.note: David Nolan takes the ride on a mare who has consistently placed at 12-14f on Soft and Standard, but the jump to Good ground and 1m7f is a double query — her sim-going record shows no wins from 15 runs on similar surfaces; naturally a hold-up horse whose true style has been pushed into a midfield slot by the field's composition.

runners_data.name: Billy No Mates
runners_data.note: A decade-old veteran who finished third at this trip on Good in his penultimate start, giving him live each-way credentials; Rhys Elliott's 5lb claim helps offset the weight, though the horse's natural instinct to close from deep places him in a physically congested part of the field given how many others share that inclination.

runners_data.name: Aighear
runners_data.note: Won and placed multiple times at 13-16f but largely on Soft and Heavier surfaces, with only one Good-ground run in this sample; Amie Waugh's 3lb claim is valuable, but the 45-day break combined with questionable Good-ground form adds uncertainty, and his true closing style means he is squeezed into midfield by the field's makeup rather than racing there naturally.

runners_data.name: Ebony Maw
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old who tends to find this sort of Good-ground surface less comfortable than Soft, having recorded just one place from four runs on similar going; Ewan Whillans' yard has returned 0/12 in the 14-day window, and the horse's deep hold-up style is neutralised by the large cluster of horses sharing the same rear-of-field instinct.

runners_data.name: Angelardo
runners_data.note: Young four-year-old with a 4/17f run on Good ground in his penultimate start as a modest positive, though wins have eluded him entirely at this level across 12 runs on comparable going; Billy Garritty rides, and while the horse is capable of placing, his natural instinct to come from deep is compromised by the sheer volume of hold-up types in this field.

runners_data.name: La Tosca
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's three-year-old is the rawest in the field by age and has her best form over 12f rather than the 1m7f demanded here; her Good-going record is the most limited with only four runs, but she has placed on that surface and Andrew Mullen's experience in staying handicaps could help her negotiate any pace collapse in the straight.

races.paceDynamic: Laravie is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner 1m7f handicap and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, she will be able to dictate a comfortable, uncontested gallop from the outset on Good turf at Ayr. Behind her, the field is stacked with hold-up types — Fleur De Mer, Billy No Mates, Ebony Maw, Aighear, Angelardo and Ned Broy are all natural closers, meaning the pace is unlikely to be truly searching and the race may set up as a test of stamina rather than a true grind. Gallus Norman and La Tosca offer the only realistic challenge from off the pace at a shorter distance through the field. This field holds more hold-up horses than the race shape can accommodate at the rear, with Fleur De Mer, Billy No Mates, Aighear, Ebony Maw and Angelardo all redistributed to midfield on the map — Laravie and Gallus Norman are those most naturally positioned to exploit their drawn roles. The overall race shape strongly favours a horse able to race prominently or track the steady pace set by Laravie, as a lone leader setting a sustainable gallop on Good ground at this trip rewards those close enough to pounce turning in, not those forced wide from deep.

scenarios.body: If the pace completely collapses in the straight and the entire rear of the field arrives in a mass finish.

watchPoints.text: Laravie's early positioning is critical — if Conor Whiteley elects to sit off the pace rather than lead, the entire race shape collapses and the moderate-pace scenario that favours her disappears completely.

The cluster of five redistributed hold-up types (Fleur De Mer, Billy No Mates, Aighear, Ebony Maw, Angelardo) will be jostling for the same ground in the rear-to-midfield section — watch for traffic problems turning into the straight that could cost one of them a genuine late run.

Gallus Norman is the most likely beneficiary if Laravie weakens in the final furlong, but Paul Mulrennan must time his challenge precisely from the rear — too far back and the 1m7f trip may not provide enough runway on a Good surface.

La Tosca's step up to 1m7f from a career high of 12f is significant — watch how she travels early; if she is unable to settle within her own comfort zone she could either fade badly or, conversely, be produced with a well-timed run if the pace is genuinely slow.

Fleur De Mer's 73-day absence and the switch to Good ground (0W from 15 sim-going runs) is a combination worth monitoring in the parade ring for fitness signals before concluding she is a major player.

races.name: Good Luck Scotland Classified Stakes

runners_data.name: Nala The Lioness
runners_data.note: Held a recent win over 12f on Soft-Fast ground and has the best recent form in the field; by nature a hold-up type but the redistribution here means she may end up racing more prominently than ideal, which tempers confidence in her finishing run landing.

runners_data.name: Another Beautiful
runners_data.note: 101 days off the track is the primary concern, and the tongue-tie plus visor headgear combination suggests connections are experimenting; only one placed run from fourteen attempts at similar going, but the step up to 14f here could unlock a bit more.

runners_data.name: Desert Quest
runners_data.note: Consistent placed-form record at 12f on Standard surfaces (four of five recent efforts placed), and the only runner with a proven record of hitting the frame on Good going; at 8 years old he likely travels well within himself and produces the same figure reliably.

runners_data.name: Falaise Blanc
runners_data.note: Showed ability with a second place at 12f on Good ground in his recent history, making him one of the more interesting runners on good going; a visor-wearing four-year-old trained by Katie Scott whose yard has gone quiet (0 from 8 in 14 days), though the redistribution to midfield means he may not get the covering hold-up run he needs.

runners_data.name: Freak Encounter
runners_data.note: Tongue-tie adds an unknown element for this four-year-old who has failed to place on Good going in three attempts; the lowest OR in the field at 44 and truly out of form (0/5/9/6/11 in recent starts), and the style-fit discount means this shape is unlikely to work for him.

runners_data.name: Is She Now
runners_data.note: A long absence of 128 days since last run (including a 46-day jockey absence flag) rings alarm bells, and her historical form at 18f and 16f suggests she is a thorough stayer who needs a genuine pace — the expected slow gallop here is the wrong shape for her.

runners_data.name: Late Claim
runners_data.note: Only one run from fifteen attempts on similar going produced a placed effort, and the seven-pound claimer Finlay Bassett may struggle with traffic in a muddled sprint finish; the style-fit discount applies as she is a natural hold-up type mapped into midfield.

runners_data.name: Tracker Issue
runners_data.note: Top-rated alongside Star Of Emerald at OR=50 and has a placed effort at 16f on Good ground; the hood suggests he has been keen in the past, and if the slow pace means he travels well before quickening, his form at longer trips on Good gives him a credible profile here.

runners_data.name: Star Of Emerald
runners_data.note: Youngest in the field at three with the lightest weight of 120lbs, trained by Edward Bethell whose yard has been active (3 from 21 in 14 days); only four career runs but placed at 12f on Good ground, and the visor is new — if it sharpens him up, he is the one most capable of producing a turn of foot in a sprint finish.

races.paceDynamic: With no confirmed front-runner in the field and every declared runner carrying a hold-up profile, this 1m5f contest at Ayr is set to crawl early before developing into a sprint-style finish from the home straight. There is no horse to press forward and set a genuine gallop, meaning the pace is likely to be false and moderate until jockeys start to ask questions entering the final two furlongs. The field holds significantly more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate naturally — Nala The Lioness, Late Claim, Falaise Blanc, Freak Encounter, and Is She Now are all redistributed in the map, and of these, Nala The Lioness and Falaise Blanc (who has recent Good-ground form at a similar trip) are most likely to be nudged forward to fill a de facto prominent role simply by virtue of circumstance rather than intent. A muddling, slowly-run affair with a compressed finish favours any runner possessing a sharp late turn of foot or proven ability to quicken off a slow pace — the profile that benefits most here is the horse who can sit handy without being restrained and quicken once the race ignites, rather than a pure closer needing a true end-to-end gallop to deliver.

watchPoints.text: Tracker Issue and Star Of Emerald share top billing at OR=50 — whichever of the two gets the clearest run through traffic in the straight is the most dangerous horse in a sprint finish.

Is She Now returns after 128 days off and has been flagged with a jockey absence — watch the market closely for any sign she has been freshened for a gamble, as that layoff and staying pedigree is an unusual fit for this shape.

Falaise Blanc has proven Good-ground ability at 12f and is trained by Katie Scott whose strike rate has dried up — if the yard sharpens up, he could outrun his price, but the redistribution to midfield means his run may get blocked in a bunched finish.

With nine hold-up types all likely converging in the straight at roughly the same time, draw and rail position leaving the final bend could be decisive — watch which jockeys position for the inner early and who is caught wide and flat in the closing stages.
